title: Single flight
hints: Two kinds of waiting are mixed up here. The mutex only protects the **map** for a moment (look up / insert / delete). Waiting for the result is done with the call's `done` channel: closing a channel wakes every goroutine receiving from it, which is exactly "tell all the waiters at once".

Start with `g.mu.Lock()`. If `c, ok := g.calls[key]` finds a call: `c.dups++`, unlock, `<-c.done`, return `c.val, true, c.err`. Otherwise create the map if nil, store `c := &call[V]{done: make(chan struct{})}`, unlock, and run `c.val, c.err = fn()` with no lock held.

After `fn` returns: `g.mu.Lock(); delete(g.calls, key); shared = c.dups > 0; g.mu.Unlock(); close(c.done); return c.val, shared, c.err`. Reading `dups` after the delete (under the lock) is safe: no one can join a call that's no longer in the map. Writing `c.val` before `close(c.done)` makes it visible to every waiter after `<-c.done`.
